messages:
maria: Quick check — RFC implementation PR #842 proposes moving the policy eval into a plugin runtime (wasm) instead of the current sidecar. Concern: added per-request hop could add 1-3ms. Thoughts?
ben: 1-3ms sounds small, but at peak that multiplies. How does this affect hedged routing latencies? :thinking_face:
kai: The PR optimizes for cold-start by caching compiled wasm per-tenant. If cache hit, we're talking ~0.5ms for dispatch + eval. Misses would be worse.
zoe: Can we quantify cache miss rate? Also important: region affinity checks currently short-circuit in sidecar — will that remain short-circuitable?
maria: Good point. PR includes an API to run a 'fast-path' prefilter in the runtime as a native callback; but that ties runtimes to host ABI. Tradeoff: purity of plugin model vs extra host bindings.
ben: If we add host ABI for fast-path, we reintroduce coupling we wanted to remove. Alternative: keep minimal host prefilter in sidecar that runs only 2-3 trivial checks (region, tier, SLA) and then call wasm for scoring.
kai: That hybrid seems practical. Sidecar prefilter keeps p99 small and wasm handles complex scoring/policy combinators.
zoe: For cost routing, we need access to recent token-cost signals (sliding window) — can wasm safely read that telemetry? Performance vs staleness tradeoff.
nate: Telemetry is currently exposed via a local memcache in sidecar. PR plans to expose a read-only snapshot at call-time to wasm via a serialized blob. Size ~ 600 bytes.
maria: 600 bytes per call is okay if we batch/inline it. But for high qps tenants it could increase CPU. We should measure.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: Canary started: policy-plugin-canary-v1 -> 10% traffic (region: us-east-1). Link: https://deploys/redwood/canary/842
ben: Can we add an opt-in flag per-tenant to force sidecar-only until they verify behavior? So enterprise tenants with strict SLAs can stay on old path.
kai: Agreed. Also add a telemetry tag to compare route choices (old vs new) for the same inputs — diff-based regression detection.
zoe: What about fallback behavior on wasm OOM or timeouts? Current sidecar has deterministic fallback to 'legacy-default' policy.
maria: PR implements a hard timeout (10ms) and a fallback to a precompiled policy stored in the host. Also circuit-breaker metrics emitted.
ben: Do we need rollout guardrails: e.g., disable on p99 latency spike >5ms, or route error rate >0.1%? We should encode that into the canary.
kai: Yep. Add automatic rollback hooks, and a nightly job that runs 1000 synthetic requests across model/region combos and compares route outputs.
zoe: For long-term, if wasm gains maturity we could push more ownership into model-specific scoring modules. But keep interface stable: input struct, snapshot telemetry, and a scoring output (score + reason codes).
maria: Action items: 1) ben add per-tenant opt-in flag + docs. 2) kai add telemetry diff tagging and nightly synthetic test. 3) zoe run perf microbench for snapshot blob sizes. 4) nate validate canary rollback thresholds. I'll update PR with these.
ben: LGTM. If perf microbench passes and telemetry diff shows negligible divergence, we can expand canary to 50% next week.
zoe: Thanks team. I'll schedule a 30m follow-up after perf results.
maria: Thanks all. :thumbsup:
